title: Tenant-aware eviction arbitration for hybrid LRU/TTL with batching safety
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As continuous batching increases throughput, the KV cache footprint on GPU memory grows non-uniformly across tenants/namespaces. Simple global LRU or TTL-only policies cause tail latency regressions and occasional incorrect reuse of stale KV entries for prefix-scoped requests. This ticket designs and implements a tenant-aware eviction arbitration layer that composes LRU + TTL + namespace affinity and guarantees correctness for in-flight batched requests while optimizing GPU memory utilization.

Goals:
- Prevent cross-tenant prefix contamination and ensure no stale KV reuse for active in-flight requests.
- Reduce out-of-memory (OOM) events during load spikes by reclaiming unpinned entries aggressively while preserving hot-path cache hits.
- Maintain low additional CPU overhead and be compatible with continuous batching and GPU slab allocation strategies.

Scope: design, implementation, integration tests, microbenchmarks, and a rollout plan with canary on Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Implementation includes a tenant/namespace lease token and eviction fence mechanism that prevents eviction of entries required by any in-flight batch.
2) Hybrid policy (LRU score + TTL penalty + tenant watermarks) is implemented and tunable via runtime knobs.
3) End-to-end correctness tests that simulate concurrent batching, prefetch, and eviction must show zero instances of stale prefix hits and consistent model outputs for pinned sequences.
4) Memory usage patterns on synthetic traffic must show at least 15% fewer OOMs compared to current baseline under bursty mix workloads, and median latency change <= +2ms.
5) Rollout plan with monitoring dashboards (cache hit rate by tenant, eviction-rate, fence-conflicts) and automatic rollback conditions documented.
comments: 2025-09-18 - Asha Patel: Created RFC sketch with high-level invariants. Proposed using a small lease token per batch to pin all KV keys referenced by that batch until batch completion or explicit release. Initial rationale: cheaper than per-query global pin and aligns with continuous batching model.

2025-09-22 - Marcus Liu: Design review notes: prefer lightweight fence IDs (64-bit) that can be stashed in the batch context; avoid blocking GPU kernels on per-key locks. Asked for a failure mode section describing what happens when the lease holder crashes mid-batch.

2025-09-25 - SRE (Elena Gomez): Observability requirements: emit fence acquisition/release events and per-tenant eviction-rate metrics. Add alert for fence-conflict-retries > 100/min. Also requested a dashboard template URL (see related_links).

2025-09-28 - Marcus Liu: Implemented eviction score: score = alpha * recency_rank + beta * ttl_penalty + gamma * tenant_watermark. Tunables exposed via runtime flags. Added soft-demerit for entries with active prefetch counters. Pushed initial prototype (PR link below).
2025-09-30 - Security (Priya Menon): Quick review: tenant fence tokens must not be replayable by unprivileged components. Marcus to add HMAC per-region in next patch.

2025-10-01 - Marcus Liu: Integration tests added. Observed a pathological case where very small tenants (few hot prefixes) were overly penalized by tenant_watermark; added fairness cap and logged behavior. Next: run Dedicated canary for 48h with bursty paraphrase workload.
2025-10-01 - Asha Patel: Added rollout runbook and rollback criteria. Scheduling canary for 2025-10-05 in eu-west-1 Dedicated pool.
